criteria.unclear: The item mentions Markdown and tracker (`br`/`bd`) plan material but does not make clear whether the plan-anchoring gate supports both as plan inputs.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly conflict with the requirement that the plan-anchoring gate accept both a Markdown plan and the corresponding plan copy in a `br` or `bd` tracker? Judge only exclusion or incompatibility with that required pair. Silence, refactoring source selection, or adding another source format is not a conflict unless the item also excludes or makes unusable Markdown or tracker (`br`/`bd`) input.

criteria.yes: The item says the gate will accept only one required source, reject or disable Markdown or tracker (`br`/`bd`) plan input, or otherwise makes it impossible to review both members of the required pair.
criteria.no: The item accepts both required sources, is silent about the pair, changes source-selection internals without excluding either source, or adds another source while leaving Markdown and tracker (`br`/`bd`) compatible.
criteria.unclear: The item may limit Markdown or tracker (`br`/`bd`) plan input, but it is not clear whether both required sources remain usable.

history.previous_statement: The plan-anchoring planning gate must accept equivalent Markdown sprint plans and bd or br tracker copies, normalize both sources to the same item contract, and return matching verdicts.
/plan-anchor must accept both a Markdown plan and its copy in a br database.
/plan-anchor must run against both a Markdown plan and its br database copy.
The plan-anchoring gate must accept both a Markdown plan and its copy in a br database.

anchors.statement: Markdown plan review requires tracker records only for an anchor root and its plan-question and dev-question children.
anchors.quote: at that point the only beads dependency in the plan is for holding the anchoring info and questions which can be spun up in a br database quickly for any repo
anchors.context: plan-anchor Phase A dogfood correction; live rubric pending explicit TypeSafe payload approval
anchors.scope: changes tracker prerequisites, anchor storage, question storage, Markdown plan review, or required issue layout
anchors.deterministic_check: Complete Markdown-source dry-run review in a repository whose tracker contains only anchor roots with plan-question and dev-question children.

pass: Markdown review reads plan text from sprint files and uses br only for each anchor's question tree.
fail: Markdown review requires the phase and every sprint to exist as br issues before it can run.

history.previous_statement: Markdown plan review must require no bd or br records beyond each anchor's standard three-record question tree.
Markdown plan review’s tracker dependency must be limited to anchor and question records.
The plan’s only Beads dependency must be anchor and question records.
Markdown plan review must require tracker records only for anchors and their question records.
The sole tracker record type required by Markdown plan review is an anchor question tree.

anchors.statement: The skill must document br initialization with no prerequisite beyond a local Git repository.
anchors.quote: at that point the only beads dependency in the plan is for holding the anchoring info and questions which can be spun up in a br database quickly for any repo
anchors.context: plan-anchor Phase A dogfood correction; live rubric pending explicit TypeSafe payload approval
anchors.scope: changes br installation, local initialization prerequisites, command examples, or onboarding
anchors.deterministic_check: Run the documented br initialization sequence in a temporary local Git repository without a remote service or phase epic.

pass: In any local Git repository, the documented br initialization commands work without a remote tracker service or a phase epic.
fail: Before br can initialize, every repository must connect to a shared tracker service and create a phase epic.

history.previous_statement: The skill must provide a short br initialization path that creates a usable anchor and question store in any Git repository.
The plan-anchoring skill must document a short br setup for its anchor and question records.
A br database for anchor and question records must be quick to initialize in any repository.
The skill must provide a documented br command sequence that initializes an anchor-and-question store in any Git repository.

anchors.statement: The harness-specific anchor-tuning agent must be a peer Opus/Sol agent that can invoke subagents while retaining tuning judgment.
anchors.quote:
I would expect anchor-tuning.md agent to be a peer agent which can call subagents.

anchor-tuning would call jev w/ a set of questions in parallel (i.e. many more questions that the final calls would use), rank the questions and down-select.
anchors.scope: changes tuning-agent hierarchy, harness model/tool access, or delegation authority
anchors.deterministic_check: Repository validation proves both harnesses register anchor-tuning.md as an Opus/Sol peer with Agent/subagent capability and reserve oracle interpretation and question-selection judgment for that coordinator.

pass: The Opus/Sol anchor-tuning peer invokes read-only Jev workers but alone freezes the oracle and selects questions.
fail: A leaf tuner without Agent access performs every Jev call sequentially and cannot dispatch subagents.

history.previous_statement: The harness-specific anchor-tuning agent must be a peer Opus/Sol coordinator that can invoke subagents, evaluate a larger candidate-question pool through parallel Jev calls against one frozen oracle, and use independent judgment to rank and down-select the production question set.

history.reason: User simplified the topology: anchor-tuning is a dedicated planner subagent that calls Jev directly; nested peer delegation is no longer required.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must rank parallel Jev evaluations of a frozen-oracle candidate pool and down-select fewer questions for production review.
anchors.quote: anchor-tuning would call jev w/ a set of questions in parallel (i.e. many more questions that the final calls would use), rank the questions and down-select.
anchors.scope: changes candidate-question generation, parallel Jev evaluation, ranking, down-selection, or production question payloads
anchors.deterministic_check: Tournament tests prove a larger candidate pool is evaluated by direct parallel Jev calls against identical frozen-oracle cases, ranking evidence and tuner rationales are retained, and production review receives only the down-selected questions.

pass: The tuner runs a broad candidate pool in parallel on one frozen oracle, records the ranking, and sends only selected questions to plan review.
fail: The production review sends every speculative tuning question because no ranked down-selection occurs.

history.previous_statement: The anchor-tuning agent must evaluate more candidate questions than production review uses by running them through Jev in parallel against one frozen oracle, ranking the evidence, and using independent judgment to down-select the production question set.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must not modify authoritative plan sources.
anchors.quote: anchor-tuning ONLY makes the plan modifications on temporary copies of the plan and does NOT modify the original plan.
anchors.summary: Authoritative plans are read-only to tuning
anchors.scope: changes tuning fixtures, mutation testing, plan-source writes, or authoritative Markdown/tracker content
anchors.deterministic_check: Mutation tests hash authoritative Markdown and tracker copies before and after tuning and prove both originals remain unchanged.

pass: The tuner leaves the Markdown plan and tracker copy byte-identical after calibration.
fail: The tuner edits the authoritative sprint document to make Jev notice a requirement.

history.previous_statement: Anchor-tuning may alter plan text only in temporary diagnostic copies and must never modify the authoritative plan.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must test candidate questions on temporary plan copies with diagnostic additions and removals.
anchors.quote: anchor-tuning is allowed to modify proposed plan text w/ added ceremony to insure jev finds it, he may also remove important statements or deliverables so jev will flag the info missing.
anchors.scope: changes tuning fixtures, candidate-question evaluation, mutation cases, or temporary workspace behavior
anchors.deterministic_check: Tuning tests create disposable positive-visibility and required-content-removal variants, derive their expected outcomes from intent and anchors, evaluate candidates against them, and delete the variants without source writes.

pass: The tuner adds explicit ceremony and removes a required deliverable only in disposable copies, then checks whether candidate questions distinguish both cases.
fail: The tuner evaluates candidates only on the unchanged plan and never proves they detect missing required content.

anchors.statement: Planning must run a named <team>-anchor-tuning subagent concurrently after the first draft and INTENT/ANC capture.
anchors.quote: planning agent puts together a first draft of the plan, launches named team-member <team>-anchor-tuning which starts refining jev questions based on intent + anchors defined in parallel w/ planner completing the plan.
anchors.scope: changes planning workflow ordering, subagent naming, tuning startup, or review prerequisites
anchors.deterministic_check: Workflow tests prove a stable <team>-anchor-tuning subagent starts after the first draft and approved INTENT/ANC authority packet, overlaps continued plan authoring, and completes before leaf plan review consumes questions.

pass: The planner launches team-a-anchor-tuning after the first draft and approved INTENT/ANC packet, then continues plan authoring while tuning runs.
fail: The planner completes the plan before starting an unnamed tuning subagent.

history.previous_statement: Planning must run a named <team>-anchor-tuning peer concurrently after the first draft and INTENT/ANC capture.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning may recommend clarity-only refinements or additions to INTENT and ANC records.
anchors.quote: Note:  anchor-tuning can also recommend refinements or additions to anchors or intent for clarity (not to change meaning).
anchors.scope: changes tuner findings, intent or anchor clarification proposals, or authority-edit boundaries
anchors.deterministic_check: Contract tests permit a recommendation envelope for clarity-only INTENT/ANC edits, require a rationale and semantic-equivalence explanation, and forbid the tuner from applying or broadening them.

pass: The tuner proposes a wording clarification with a rationale showing that the INTENT/ANC meaning is unchanged.
fail: The tuner proposes a new product constraint as a clarification to an existing anchor.

anchors.statement: The user must approve every anchor-tuning recommendation before INTENT or ANC records are changed.
anchors.quote: user should be consulted w/ recommended refinements to ANC + INTENT.
anchors.scope: changes approval handling, intent or anchor updates, oracle invalidation, or tuning restart behavior
anchors.deterministic_check: Workflow tests prove recommended authority edits remain proposals until explicit user approval; an approved version change invalidates and reruns affected oracles and candidate rankings.

pass: The tuner presents its clarification proposal to the user and waits; after approval, the affected authority version and tournament are refreshed.
fail: The tuner directly edits INTENT and keeps using the old oracle without asking the user.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must run as a dedicated Opus/Sol subagent of the planner.
anchors.quote: I suppose anchor-tuning could simply be a sub-agent of planner (opus/sol minimum)
anchors.scope: changes tuning-agent hierarchy, launch ownership, or tuner model selection
anchors.deterministic_check: Harness contract tests prove the planner launches the dedicated anchor-tuning profile with Opus on Claude and Sol on Codex, using an isolated structured authority packet.

pass: The planner launches the isolated anchor-tuning profile with Opus or Sol and a structured INTENT/ANC authority packet.
fail: The planner itself rewrites Jev questions in its own context.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must run its candidate-question Jev evaluations directly.
anchors.quote: he could run jev questions directly.
anchors.scope: changes candidate-question execution, Jev call ownership, or nested-agent delegation
anchors.deterministic_check: Execution traces prove anchor-tuning invokes Jev directly for its parallel candidate pool and does not require nested Agent delegation.

pass: Anchor-tuning directly launches parallel Jev calls for its candidate pool and records every result.
fail: Anchor-tuning must spawn nested Agent workers before it can evaluate any candidate question.

anchors.statement: After anchor-plan-review, the planner must fix genuine plan findings or send raw review evidence to anchor-tuning for question-defect triage.
anchors.quote: planner would then send results of anchor-plan-review to anchor-tuning and/or update his plan to fix issues found.
anchors.scope: changes post-review triage, plan repair, question retuning, or review-result routing
anchors.deterministic_check: Workflow tests route genuine findings to planner-owned plan edits and suspected question defects as unmodified review evidence to anchor-tuning; tuner triage cannot receive a desired verdict.

pass: The planner fixes a confirmed missing deliverable, while a suspicious low-confidence role answer is sent unchanged to anchor-tuning for oracle-based triage.
fail: The planner asks anchor-tuning to rewrite a question until a failing plan review passes.

anchors.statement: Planner-to-anchor-tuning review feedback must be rendered from a checked-in sc-compose Jinja2 template.
anchors.quote: with this work model, it is important that the feedback sent to anchor-tuning be in a sc-compose j2 template which has strong wording that his job is NOT to fix jev failures that accurately point out issues w/ the current plan.
anchors.summary: Render planner feedback through checked-in sc-compose template
anchors.scope: Planner-to-anchor-tuning review feedback transport.
anchors.deterministic_check: Validate the checked-in .j2 template with sc-compose --strict and prove the planner renders every review-feedback handoff from it.

pass: The planner renders the raw review request and result through the checked-in anchor-tuning-review-feedback.md.j2 template with sc-compose --strict.
fail: The planner writes a free-form message asking the tuner to fix questions.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must independently classify each disputed Jev failure as either a cited plan violation or a cited question defect.
anchors.quote: the anchor-tuning should respond w/ a) your plan violates ANC-XXX or INTENT-YYY. OR b) Yes, jev's response does not support ANC-XXX or INTENT-YYY, I will update the questions.
anchors.scope: Anchor-tuning triage of planner-submitted Jev failures.
anchors.deterministic_check: Reject triage results unless disposition is plan_violation or question_defect and evidence cites at least one approved ANC or INTENT identifier.

pass: The tuner returns plan_violation, cites ANC-010, quotes the conflicting plan text, and leaves the sealed question digest unchanged.
The tuner returns question_defect, cites INTENT review policy, shows the frozen-oracle mismatch, and reopens the affected question tournament.
fail: The tuner accepts the planner conclusion and edits the question without choosing a disposition or citing authority.

anchors.statement: Anchor-tuning must not change an accurate Jev question merely because the planner asks it to make a failing plan pass.
anchors.quote: the feedback path from planner -> anchor-tuning has risk that planner would say 'jev is failing by plan, fix the questions'.
anchors.summary: Forbid pass-seeking retuning from planner pressure
anchors.scope: Anchor-tuning triage and question updates after plan review.
anchors.deterministic_check: Mutation tests submit a planner request to fix questions for a known plan defect and require plan_violation with unchanged sealed question digest.

pass: A planner asks to fix a question for a known plan defect; the tuner rejects the request as plan_violation and preserves the sealed question digest.
fail: A planner says the plan must pass, so the tuner weakens an accurate question until Jev returns pass.

anchors.statement: A plan-anchor install rendered for one tracker must not name the other tracker as a whole word in any installed file except references/installation-and-troubleshooting.md.
anchors.quote:
I expect that installing 'bd' will ONLY have 'bd' commands in md files and scripts.  alternatively installing 'br' will ONLY have 'br' in md and scripts.

bd and br should both be in installation & troubleshooting guide since  the install guide should explain how this switch works.
anchors.context: plan-anchor 0.8.2 tracker-pure installs (operator, relayed by the coordinating agent)
anchors.scope: changes install templates, the files install.py copies or renders, tracker-specific text or code in scripts, or the install guide
anchors.deterministic_check: Fresh install.py run per tracker with --target claude,codex,cursor; grep -rnwI <other tracker> over .claude .codex .cursor .sc finds lines only in references/installation-and-troubleshooting.md (test_install.py::RealInstallTests.test_each_install_names_only_its_tracker).

pass: The sprint renders jev_judge.py from jev_judge.py.j2 so a br install's help text says 'br show --json' and never names bd.
fail: The sprint keeps scripts copied verbatim, so a br install's jev_judge.py still tells the user to run 'bd children'.

anchors.statement: Rerunning install.py with the other --tracker over an existing install must leave a folder byte-identical to a fresh install of that tracker, in both directions.
anchors.quote: installing 'br' then installing 'bd' on top of it will look EXACTLY the same as just installing 'bd' in an empty location.  likewise for the opposite.
anchors.context: plan-anchor 0.8.2 tracker-pure installs (operator, relayed by the coordinating agent)
anchors.scope: changes tracker switching, the lock file, settings writes, file ownership or removal, or rendering in install.py
anchors.deterministic_check: Install br then bd (and bd then br) for every target and compare with a fresh install of the second tracker: identical file lists, bytes and modes, lock and settings included (test_install.py::RealInstallTests.test_switching_trackers_equals_a_fresh_install).

pass: The sprint checks that a br install switched to bd matches a fresh bd install byte for byte, lock and settings included, and the reverse.
fail: After a switch the old tracker's rendered scripts and settings comments stay behind, so the folder differs from a fresh install.

anchors.statement: Every Markdown file and Python script that install.py installs must be rendered at install time from a <file>.md.j2 or <script>.py.j2 template under install/templates/.
anchors.quote: I expect the markdown files and scripts are <file>.md.j2 and <script>.py.j2 and are rendered when installed.
anchors.context: plan-anchor 0.8.2 tracker-pure installs (operator, relayed by the coordinating agent)
anchors.summary: Installed md and py rendered from .j2
anchors.scope: adds, moves or copies an installed Markdown file or script, or changes how install.py renders or copies files
anchors.deterministic_check: Every installed .md and .py traces to an install template whose frontmatter name starts with sc-plan-anchor- (test_install.py::RealInstallTests.test_every_installed_md_and_py_is_rendered_from_a_template, RenderingTests.test_every_prompt_source_is_a_template).

pass: Each script moves to scripts/<name>.py.j2 and install.py renders it for the selected tracker like every reference.
fail: The scripts stay plain .py files that install.py copies unchanged into every install.

anchors.statement: The sc-plan-anchor plugin must expose only the plan-anchor-installer skill, with no loadable plan-anchoring skill and no agents.
anchors.quote: the ENTIRE reason we changed to ONLY advertising plan-anchor-installer and hiding plan anchor was what I outlined above.
anchors.context: plan-anchor 0.8.2 tracker-pure installs (operator, relayed by the coordinating agent)
anchors.scope: changes the plugin's skills/ or agents directories, plugin or marketplace manifests, or what the marketplace plugin ships
anchors.deterministic_check: plugins/sc-plan-anchor/skills/ holds only plan-anchor-installer and no .claude, .codex, .cursor or skills/plan-anchoring tree exists in the plugin (test_install.py::RenderingTests.test_plugin_ships_only_the_installer_skill_and_no_rendered_tree).

pass: The marketplace plugin's skills/ directory holds only plan-anchor-installer; plan-anchoring and its agents exist only in per-folder installs.
fail: The plugin advertises the plan-anchoring skill and its agents again so a marketplace install can run the gates directly.

anchors.statement: install.py must refuse a --dest inside the global ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor or ~/.agents folders with INSTALL.DEST_GLOBAL and write nothing.
anchors.quote: we also block installing 'plan-anchor' in global .claude, .codex, .cursor, .agents folders
anchors.context: plan-anchor 0.8.2 tracker-pure installs (operator, relayed by the coordinating agent)
anchors.scope: changes install.py destination checks, plan_anchor_paths.global_location, or the installer skill's destination handling
anchors.deterministic_check: install.py --dest ~/.claude (and .codex, .cursor, .agents and their subfolders) exits 2 with INSTALL.DEST_GLOBAL and leaves the tree unchanged (test_installer_skill.py::GlobalDestinationTests).

pass: install.py --dest ~/.codex exits 2 with INSTALL.DEST_GLOBAL and writes no file.
fail: install.py accepts --dest ~/.claude and writes a shared plan-anchoring skill there for every repository.
